both dispatch arms pin hold_tests._configure(..., session_slots=0) at :407 and :425, so only the lane-held path is exercised, and the free-lane case the previous review's first finding is about has no arm at all; the manifest's own follow_ons admits the free-lane arm was written, failed and removed rather than left red, which leaves the claim in the code comment at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1716 ('whatever the lane state') resting on a reading and not on a gate - the removal is the defect the record itself names, since a red arm that was deleted is indistinguishable from a case that was never covered.

the node's own commit adds lint findings in a repo whose rule is that a commit adds none: '_request_state' imports COMPLETED_STATUSES and TERMINAL_STATUSES and uses neither, and the new test module carries three E402 and one FURB167 - eight findings across the changed paths, four of them in code this node created.

queue_requests, the batch entry point plan section 2's 'queue a whole width in one call' needs, still has no production caller - grep over reckon/ and skills/ finds it only in the new test module, and the dispatch path reaches the hold per node - so the batch half is provable but inert until a queue verb lands; the same gap was recorded by the previous review at :1347 and it is unchanged at this head.

plan section 2 names the watch stream among the readers that must take the phase words from the vocabulary, and it does not: RECOVERY_VERBS and reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py carry neither 'awaiting-upstream' nor 'blocked-upstream', so a held request is drawn on no watch line; the file is outside the node's fence and the manifest records it under follow_ons, so the gap is disclosed and the fence rather than the worker holds it.
